messages:
Julia: Customer flagged a transitive CVE in our on-prem agent; they want SBOM, remediation ETA, and KMS rotation guidance. They asked whether we can rollback the agent or provide an allowlist as a temporary mitigation. Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-1234
Sarah: Can you paste the exact agent version and the dependency path? Is this their managed tenant or a self-hosted VPC?
Julia: Agent version 2.0.1. Dependency path: redwood-agent -> telemetry-lib -> netparser@1.4.0. This is a self-hosted VPC with KMS integration for secret encryption. Upstream advisory: https://github.com/netparser/security-advisory#CVE-2026-1234
Mike: Quick upstream check: netparser patched this in v1.4.2. No public API changes. The fix is a safe drop-in but requires the agent process to restart to pick up the updated artifact. We can cut a hotfix agent release 2.0.2 that bumps netparser.
Sarah: Triage summary: exploitability = medium (crafted egress payload to ingestion), impact scope = local ingestion pipeline. Because this customer runs private infra with KMS-bound keys, mark it high priority for that tenant. Proposed remediation SLA = 48-72h unless they request immediate patch.
Julia: They need SOC2/contract evidence: SBOM export, remediation timeline with actor timestamps, audit logs showing upgrade and any KMS ops, and a written mitigation plan if we can't patch within their window. Also asked whether keys require rotation.
Oliver: For evidence we can export SBOM (SPDX + CycloneDX) and the Console audit CSV (Activity -> Export). We can include the release artifact checksum and sign a remediation letter. Support can provide the audit slice for that tenant. ETA for a signed statement: end of day tomorrow if Security drafts the bullet points.
Sarah: I'll assemble an evidence bundle containing: 1) SBOM (spdx + cyclonedx) 2) CVE mapping + patch notes 3) remediation timeline template 4) KMS rotation playbook excerpt 5) verification commands and checksums. Example SBOM command:
```
./scripts/generate_sbom.sh --format spdx --component "redwood-agent@2.0.1" > sbom-agent-2.0.1.spdx
```
Mike: Proposed rollout for the customer: build 2.0.2 (bump netparser), run smoke in staging, then rolling restart of agent processes in their cluster. Estimate: ~2h build+CI, ~1h rollout (size-dependent). Recommend 10% canary first, then ramp. We'll include a package SHA256 in the signed note.
Sarah: Temporary mitigations while patching: 1) allowlist/block egress patterns that trigger the vuln 2) disable optional telemetry parser via feature flag 3) WAF/network rule on ingress if they have one. About KMS: rotation is not strictly required unless there is evidence of key compromise; still provide the rotation playbook and offer to coordinate rotation.
Julia: Customer also asked for timestamped proof that we performed the upgrade and any KMS actions. How granular are our audit exports?
Oliver: Console audit export includes actor, action, timestamp, resource; Support can export activity for the tenant and attach it to the bundle. We can also publish release artifact hash and the agent binary checksum for verification. That meets SOC2 evidence needs.
Support: We can slice audit logs for the tenant and generate a CSV with these columns: timestamp, actor, action, resource, details. We'll redact unrelated org data.
deploy-bot: build triggered: redwood-agent/2.0.2 (#345) by Mike — CI passed.
Mike: Build artifacts uploaded. Package sha256: 6d4f8b9a2c3e... (full hash in artifact registry). Preparing release notes and the hotfix tag.
Julia: I'll send the evidence bundle to the customer and ask whether they want us to coordinate KMS rotation. Will update thread after their response. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Sarah: On it. I'll also update the vulnerability tracker: CVE-2026-1234, customer impacted, mitigation assigned to @Mike, target patch window = 48h.
Julia: Ping me when the bundle link is ready and when the signed statement PDF is uploaded.
